# Workflow {.unnumbered}

## Before fieldwork:

Print enough field sheets for wood core sample collection and leaf sample collection. The template of these files can be found here:

**Field sheets**

XLSX: [field_sheet.xlsx](documents/field_sheet.xlsx)

PDF: [field_sheet.pdf](documents/field_sheet.pdf) [TO DO: update if agreement on the xlsx]{style="color: red;"}

**Species codes**

Belterra XLSX: [field_code_Belterra.xlsx](documents/field_code_Belterra.xlsx)

Belterra PDF: [field_code_Belterra.pdf](documents/field_code_Belterra.pdf)

Print several maps of the trees.

## Before starting a lab work day:

Prepare the following files:

**Osmometer measurements**

`TLP_YYYYMMDD.xlsx` : an excel file per day to record the osmometer measurements. Make one file per day so it can be saved every evening, with the date format as follow: ex `TLP_20270120.xlsx`. The template of this file can be found here :

Link English 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 : [template_TLP_YYYYMMDD.xlsx](documents/template_TLP_YYYYMMDD.xlsx)

```{r}
readxl::read_xlsx("documents/template_TLP_YYYYMMDD.xlsx") |> 
  knitr::kable()
```

**Hydrated leaves measurements**

`HYD_YYYYMMDD.xls` : an excel file per day to record the fresh leaf measurements (thickness, weight and scan done). Make one file per day so it can be saved every evening, with the date format as follow: ex `HYD_20270120.xls`. The template of this file can be found here :

Link English 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 : [template_HYD_YYYYMMDD.xls](documents/template_HYD_YYYYMMDD.xls)

```{r}
readxl::read_xls("documents/template_HYD_YYYYMMDD.xls") |> 
  knitr::kable()
```

**Dry leaves measurements**

`DRY_YYYYMMDD.xlsx` : an excel file per day to record the dry leaf weight. Make one file per day so it can be saved every evening (although the weighting will be done after oven drying), with the date format as follow: ex `DRY_20270120_dry.xlsx`). The template of this file can be found here :

Link English 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 : [template_DRY_YYYYMMDD.xlsx](documents/template_DRY_YYYYMMDD.xlsx)

```{r}
readxl::read_xlsx("documents/template_DRY_YYYYMMDD.xlsx") |> 
  knitr::kable()
```

**Leaf scans**

At the start of the day create a folder named `SCANYYYYMMDD` (ex: `SCAN20270120`) to save all leaf scans. Then inside, save each scan as `CODE_TREE_LEAF.pdf` such as `ANGEL_5663_1.pdf`.

## Every evening during field and lab work 

### List and check the samples

Record the individuals on which samples (leaf and wood) have been taken in `sample_taken.xlsx` before putting them in the oven (which allows checking that all the samples are put in the oven). Make one single file per day so it can be saved every evening, with the date format as follow `sample_taken_YYYYMMDD.xlsx` (ex `sample_taken_20270120.xlsx`), but increment the file of the previous day so that a single file contains all the samples taken since the beginning of the campaign. This file will be useful to prepare the next field day.
The template of this file can be found here:

Link English 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 : [template_sample_taken.xlsx](documents/template_sample_taken.xlsx)

```{r}
readxl::read_xlsx("documents/template_sample_taken.xlsx") |> 
  knitr::kable()
```

### Scan the field sheets

At the end of each day, scan the field sheets of the day and save them as a file named `wood_field_sheet_YYYYMMDD.pdf` (for wood samples) or `leaf_field_sheet_YYYYMMDD.pdf` (for leaf samples).

### Inspect the scans {#inspect_scan}

If time allow, process the leaf scans (following this [procedure](12_protocols.qmd#scan_processing) and inspect them manually to detect scan problems. If this is done on the day, a new scan can be redone if relevant. 

Record the manual inspection of the leaf scan in a file called  `scan_inspection_YYYYMMDD.xlsx` (ex: `scan_inspection_20270120.xlsx`), following the procedure detailled below.
The template of this file can be found here:

Link English 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 : [template_scan_inspection.xlsx](documents/template_scan_inspection.xlsx)

```{r}
readxl::read_xlsx("documents/template_scan_inspection.xlsx") |> 
  knitr::kable()
```

Here is the list of problems that should be looked for, and how to code them: 

- *missing_part*: missing part in the leave due to herbivory or other damage. This can be seen on the **mask or the raw scan**:

  - *0*: no missing part

  - *1*: moderate missing part

  - *2*: big missing part

- *anomaly*: any anomaly in the generated **masks**:

  - *ok*: no problem

  - *miss_petiolul*: for compound leaves, the petiolule is not included, while it should have been according to the protocol

  - *petiol_included*: the petiole has been included, while it should have been according to the protocol

  - *one_fol*: just one foliole when the species has compound leaves

  - *abn_area*: abnormal area, detected because they don't have the shape of a leaf. Generally, it is because these areas correspond to some spaces between the folioles that are fully surrounded by leaf part, which are interpreted as holes and filled.

::: {layout-ncol="3"}
![](documents/Belterra_2025/ANGEL_5677_5_mask.png)

![](documents/Belterra_2025/FAVAO_5685_2_mask.png)

![](documents/Belterra_2025/COPAI_6897_4._mask.png)
:::

- *touching*: leaf touching the edges of the scan, observed on the **mask**:

  - *0* no part touching (all the leaf is coloured)

  - *1* leaf touching leading to part of the leaf not taken into account (only a part of the leaf is coloured),

  - *2* leaf touching leading to all the leaf not taken into account (the whole leaf is white)
  
::: {layout-ncol="3"}
![touching = 0](documents/Belterra_2025/PEQUI_5953_3_mask.png)

![touching = 1](documents/Belterra_2025/ANGEL_5677_1_mask.png)

![touching = 2](documents/Belterra_2025/ANGEL_5677_2_mask.png)
:::

- *raw scan*: problem seen on the **raw scans**

  - *ok*: no problem (or very small area concerns)

  - *damaged*: part of the leaf or the whole leaf appears black/brown or yellowish on the scan or there are any other damages (except missing part of the leaf) suggesting that the leaf is decaying or is attacked by insects

  - *young*: the bright green colour of the leave compared to the other leaves from the individual and/or the species suggest non mature leaves
  
::: {layout-ncol="3"}
![ok](documents/Belterra_2025/CASTA_6568_4.png)

![damaged](documents/Belterra_2025/CASTA_6617_4.png)

![young](documents/Belterra_2025/VIROL_6404_3.png)
:::
  

### Save the files {#saving_files}

At the end of **every day**, data files, field sheets and scans should be saved locally in multiple places: on the computer that was used for recording, on a computer that will stored all data files, and on a USB stick/hard drive.
In addition, if the access to the cloud allows, data files, field sheets and scans can be stored every evening on the NAS ([TO DO: add link to the NAS when ok with Romain]{style="color: red;"}).

The following file structure should be used for the "central computer" and the USB stick/hard drive:

- `dry_weight/` the leaf dry weights
- `hydrated/` the leaf hydrated measurements
- `field_sheets/` the sampling field sheets in pdf names with the day and the type of
- `osmo/` the leaf hydrated measurements with osmometer
- `scans/` the leaf hydrated scans
- `sample_taken/`the list of wood and leaf samples taken


### Prepare the next field day

Based on the planned sampling, the samples already done and the map, decide which tree should be collected the next day, for leaf and wood.

## After field and lab work

### Save the raw data files on the NAS

If this was not done at the end of each day, save all the files on the NAS ([TO DO: add link to the NAS when ok with Romain]{style="color: red;"}), following the [structure described above](#saving_files).
Once all the raw data files of a campaign have been saved on the NAS; lock the folder in *read only* mode (in Properties).

If this was not done at the end of each day, manually inspect the leaf scans, following the [procedure described above](#inspect_scan).

### Clean and save the cleaned data

Do the data cleaning in the [functional repository](https://github.com/PlantForAdapt/functional)

* Data should be stored on the repository following the structure described [here](data/README.md)

* Data cleaning should be done in different group of pages for each field campaign (the Belterra 2025 campaign, or another campaign can be used as a basis for cleaning).

* A cleaned data file per campaign should be created in the folder output, and named as trait_PlantForAdapt_Site_year_vX.csv (single level versioning). Versioning of the data files is documented in the NEWS file [here](outputs/NEWS.md). Metadata are described in the README file [here](outputs/README.md). Column naming should be coherent between field campaign. If needed, the metadata file can be incremented.

* Output files (the clean data file and the updated `NEWS.md` and `README.md` files) should be saved on the NAS, in `/functional/output/` and put in *read only* mode.
